fullPassage: (A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed. (D) When Emma lost focus, it was difficult for Sandy to teach her or the other six students in the reading group. Sandy spent a lot of time thinking about how she could help Emma keep her focus and be successful. After much reflection, she decided to get her impression of how the reading group was going. When they met later that week, Emma said something that really surprised her. Emma shared that she felt like Sandy needed to be more patient with her when she sounded out words she was reading to the group. Emma knew she was not good at it, and it made her nervous and want to get away from the group. (B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one. (C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books!

(가) Emma의 읽기 그룹에는 총 7명의 학생이 있었다.
(나) Sandy는 Emma에게 책을 직접 골라 주었다.
(다) Emma는 결국 자신감을 얻어 다른 책도 읽고 싶어 했다.

det.correct: ③ T-F-T: (가) Emma+6명=7명=T (나) let Emma select(Emma가 선택)=F (다) newfound confidence=T
det.tip: (나) Sandy가 골라준 것이 아니라 Emma가 직접 선택(let Emma select)

questions.passage: (A) Sandy Robinson was a teacher in an elementary school. In addition to a variety of other duties, every afternoon Sandy worked with small groups of third graders who were reading below grade level. The goal was to raise the reading level of the students with whom she worked to help enable her school to ascend from its "academic emergency" status under the state's education rules. Emma was in one of Sandy's afternoon reading groups, and she was not improving. She lacked patience and often lost focus, at which point she became disruptive, primarily to amuse herself, or so it seemed. (D) When Emma lost focus, it was difficult for Sandy to teach her or the other six students in the reading group. Sandy spent a lot of time thinking about how she could help Emma keep her focus and be successful. After much reflection, she decided to get her impression of how the reading group was going. When they met later that week, Emma said something that really surprised her. Emma shared that she felt like Sandy needed to be more patient with her when she sounded out words she was reading to the group. Emma knew she was not good at it, and it made her nervous and want to get away from the group. (B) That evening after school, Sandy reflected on what Emma had said. Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words. The next day, Sandy told her she would meet her for some one-on-one reading instruction in addition to the small-group time. In those one-on-one meetings, Sandy let Emma select a book from a handful of books that were at her reading level. Then Sandy would read a paragraph out loud and have Emma read one. (C) They would continue to swap back and forth. Slowly but surely, they saw improvement. Over time, they were able to increase the reading level of the books as Emma's ability to sound out words improved. Sandy also noticed that Emma came to reading group with her classmates and started to make it through the entire lesson without becoming disruptive or feeling anxious. More than anything, her newfound confidence made her want to try and read other books!
questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 학생의 관점을 경청하고 맞춤 지도로 읽기 능력을 향상시킨 교사
소그룹 학습에서 발생하는 학생 갈등의 해결 방법
학업 비상 상태 학교의 교육 정책 개선 사례

det.correct: ① Sandy의 경청 → 맞춤 지도 → Emma 향상
wrongs: ③ ❌ — 갈등 해결이 아닌 학습 어려움

questions.stem: 이 글이 시사하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 학생의 학업 성취는 타고난 능력에 의해 결정된다.
교사는 항상 자신의 방법을 고수하는 것이 좋다.
소그룹 수업은 어떤 경우에도 일대일 수업보다 효과적이다.
학생의 어려움을 이해하고 맞춤형으로 접근하면 학습 향상이 가능하다.

det.correct: ④ Emma의 입장 이해 + 맞춤 수업 = 향상

밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.

<u>Sandy recalled research suggesting she needed to increase the number of words Emma was reading to improve her ability to sound out words.</u>
questions.wa: Sandy는 Emma의 단어 소리 내어 읽기 능력을 향상시키기 위해 Emma가 읽는 단어 수를 늘려야 한다고 제안하는 연구를 떠올렸다.
accept: Sandy는 Emma의 단어 소리 내어 읽기 능력을 향상시키기 위해 Emma가 읽는 단어 수를 늘려야 한다고 제안하는 연구를 떠올렸다
Sandy는 Emma가 읽는 단어 수를 늘려 읽기 능력을 향상시켜야 한다는 연구를 기억해 냈다
Sandy는 Emma의 음독 능력 향상을 위해 읽는 단어량을 늘려야 한다는 연구를 상기했다

det.correct: 연구에 따르면 읽는 단어 수를 늘리면 음독 능력이 향상된다
det.tip: recall(떠올리다), suggesting(제안하는), sound out(소리 내어 읽다)
